svg.title: House renovation workflow
svg.desc: Room design decisions with correction loops. The full guide includes each stage, homeowner questions, specialist triggers, scoped issues and a worked support-beam example.
svg.text: Review gates, return paths and homeowner decisions
Begin a private revision, check the actual work and save it. Publication follows verified backup.
Open CHECKLIST.md with the history and reviews. Check outstanding surveys and design holds.

svg.text: Issue a finding and next site check when the evidence answers the buyer’s question.
Issue the checked plan or measured hold after occupied review. Later visual stages stay pending or held.
Reopen linked rooms, orders, costs and phases when a shared decision changes.

g.text: Find a review or specialist study
Route a new question from any stage

svg.text: Read the request alongside the brief and current findings. An ordinary phrase, a changed product or a
measurement from site can introduce a specialist question.
Changed assumption or unresolved fit? Return to the affected decision and retest.

g.text: Brief, permissions and revisions

g.aria-label: Brief · Do we know enough for the next decision?
g.text: BRIEF
Do we know enough for the next decision?
On a new house, preserve the original brief, plans and photos. Create CHECKLIST.md at intake. On resuming,
read it with history, dashboard, brief, decisions and room reviews. Record household routines, shared seats
and routes, retained pieces, shopping, budget and commissioned outputs.
Tools in use
Renovation Pack and house.py start, list and add-room capture the original sources, household
routines and budget. The checklist, status and history commands bring survey evidence and
outstanding reviews together.
Proceed
Pass the brief for the relevant study. A buyer or
desk assessment can finish with the evidence,
uncertainty and next viewing or survey check. A
whole-house commission also opens the shared
decision record.
Buyer assessment
Hold, correct and return
If sources conflict, retain observed fabric in
the baseline. Identify the evidence that could
settle the conflict. Work on independent rooms or
the retained option while it is open.
Who decides
Ask the homeowner only about a gap that changes what happens next. Which activities must work
together? What must stay, what may move, and which choices may the agent make?

g.aria-label: Scope · May we explore this particular change?
g.text: SCOPE
May we explore this particular change?
Read house limits and room exceptions on both sides of a shared route. Check the budget or disruption
conditions attached to any permission. Screen each new request, follow-up or changed constraint for an
explicit or implied specialist question.
Tools in use
Renovation Pack checks household permissions against the room brief. Use house.py next, ask and
answer to show the labelled choice and record the decision.
Proceed
Explore a permitted change. For a triggered
specialist study, give its owner the question,
source revision and allowed options. Return the
finding to the relevant decision and rerun the
affected checks.
Hold, correct and return
Keep a protected item or ruled-out intervention
in place. Try a permitted alternative. Where
permission is unknown, continue the baseline.
Permission to compare an option still leaves its
selection open.
Who decides
If the owner reserved the choice, show the benefit, drawback and affected rooms before
modelling. “Keeping this doorway narrows the route. Would you like to compare moving it?”
Record the answer and its limits.

g.aria-label: Revision · Is the evidence safe to publish?
g.text: REVISION
Is the evidence safe to publish?
For each new or revised output, use begin-revision. Capture the governing instructions and inputs. Work in
the printed private directory, reopen the result and inspect it in its owning tool. If MCP disconnects,
reconnect and inspect the actual document before retrying.
Tools in use
Use house.py begin-revision, save-revision and verify-revision to preserve inputs, outputs and
their history. The backup and restore commands support recovery.
Proceed
Use save-revision with inputs, change, reason,
author, effects and next action. The save
verifies a whole-house backup before publication.
Link the saved output to the review. Report a
failed design as a measured finding.
Saved output
Hold, correct and return
If backup verification fails, keep the draft,
correct the cause and retry the same save. If
published evidence changes or the wrong revision
is supplied, hold its review, recover or create a
new revision, and recheck dependent outputs.
Who decides
The agent resolves file, connector and backup problems. Seek an owner decision only if
resolving the work would change the brief. On another computer, restore the matching house
backup to open private files.
Existing building and occupied proposal

g.aria-label: Existing CAD · Does the saved shell fit the sources?
g.text: EXISTING CAD
Does the saved shell fit the sources?
FreeCAD MCP reopens the baseline. Compare scale, axes, storeys, openings, stairs, services and obstructions
with photos, plan and sections. Mark provisional measurements. Assess actual routes through occupied
thresholds and report their limiting pinch.
Tools in use
FreeCAD MCP builds and reopens the measured shell. BIM and TechDraw show levels, openings and
sections. IfcOpenShell checks supplied IFC units and placement. Resolve survey discrepancies
against the original evidence.
Proceed
Pass existing-cad for the intended decision. A
measured assessment may end here. A proposal uses
its own revision. An optional unrendered
furniture study can branch off the checked shell.
Buyer assessment
Hold, correct and return
Correct missing or wrongly placed fabric in
existing CAD and reopen the model. If a missing
dimension could reverse the fit, record the
measurement needed and hold that fit. A concept
image cannot authorise removal of observed
fabric.
Who decides
The surveyor establishes a disputed dimension or concealed condition. Ask the homeowner before
exploring a change to retained fabric unless the relevant permission is already recorded.

g.aria-label: Furniture study · Is an unrendered study useful and permitted?
g.text: FURNITURE STUDY
Is an unrendered study useful and permitted?
Run check-study with the actual shell revision and inspect the visual instructions. A render-only hold
permits an otherwise authorised viewport study. CAD-only or all-visual instructions keep exploration in
FreeCAD.
Tools in use
Run house.py check-study on the shell revision. Blender MCP places dimensioned furniture in the
unrendered scene. The room asset library builds each candidate at its stated size and reads the
size back. Return candidate positions to FreeCAD for the occupied test.
Proceed
Blender MCP locks the transferred shell and
checks units, orientation and two landmarks. Try
placements at the entrance and seated eye height.
Return item IDs, positions, rotations, fronts and
units to proposed FreeCAD.
Hold, correct and return
For a stale shell, reversed transfer or incorrect
scale, correct the transfer and repeat the check.
If the study is outside scope, proceed directly
to permitted CAD work. A candidate still needs an
occupied layout review.
Who decides
If the use of a seat changes the decision, ask who needs the view, conversation or reach. The
agent can try arrangements within the existing permission without another approval.

g.aria-label: Proposed CAD · Does the whole room work in use?
g.text: PROPOSED CAD
Does the whole room work in use?
On one reopened CAD plan show intent, use, journey and whole-room findings together. Test every declared
position, actual shared furniture outline, operating fronts, seat views, reach, door swings and simultaneous
routes. Check sections for height. Compare permitted options on the same routine. For a highly glazed space,
review external shadows, seated glare, summer heat and winter cold before furnishing.
Tools in use
FreeCAD MCP and TechDraw show the occupied plan and sections. Shapely and GEOS measure
clearances. NetworkX traces connected journeys. Use check-routes, check-openings and
check-layout against the current geometry.
Proceed
Record the selected option or delegated choice.
Pass proposed-cad and run check-layout with the
actual revision. Issue a checked CAD-only plan if
commissioned. A diagnostic issue can show a
failed option and the measured reason for its
hold.
CAD-only issue
Hold, correct and return
On a pinch, try the least disruptive permitted
adjustment, then repeat the occupied check and
linked room journeys. A specialist’s returned
support, threshold, service or product size
reopens the same checks and any dependent quote
or order.
Who decides
Use house.py ask to check the labelled occupied plan and present it inline with the question.
“Would you prefer to keep this cabinet or pass behind eight diners?” Mark both options on the
plan. Record the reply or the measurement that will settle it, then retest.
Furnishing, colour and final photography

g.aria-label: Visual permission · Can this camera be furnished and rendered?
g.text: VISUAL PERMISSION
Can this camera be furnished and rendered?
Check the actual selected revision, current look and homeowner holds. Run check-render for blender before the
furnished camera. A render hold pauses rendered cameras, AI and publication. A broader visual hold also
pauses viewport work.
Tools in use
Renovation Pack reads the homeowner’s scope and house.py check-render checks the input revision
and render hold before the camera or final image.
Proceed
With the fit accepted, look agreed and render
released, furnish the full room in Blender. Where
the look is open, use permitted swatches, colour
advice or an authorised styling study before
sourcing.
Hold, correct and return
Keep a held visual pending. Return a changed item
to the shopping schedule and native scene. If its
fit, access or use changes, return to occupied
CAD, then repeat transfer and camera checks.
Who decides
“Which of these finishes should we carry forward?” Use an existing delegation where it covers
the choice. If the homeowner paused a visual, record the release for that particular work
before resuming.

g.aria-label: Blender · Does the reopened camera show the selected room?
g.text: BLENDER
Does the reopened camera show the selected room?
Match CAD units, axes, two identifiable features, boundaries and openings. Trace each seat approach and exit
with adjacent places occupied. Test plants, door travel and cupboard access. Once the walkthrough passes,
render and inspect the named camera and reverse view for placement, clipping, hidden items and light.
Tools in use
Blender MCP places and counts the selected objects. A room asset library stand-in represents a
selected product only where it matches that product's distinctive form. After the last
accessory, reopen the scene. Living in the Room uses the route solver and opening measurements
before the camera is rendered.
Proceed
Pass the blender review for that scene and
camera. Pass the named object list, reviewed
camera, reverse view and asset provenance to the
product review.
Hold, correct and return
Correct a transfer, misplaced object, incomplete
dressing or clipped view in Blender. If the
source opening or selected arrangement is wrong,
correct existing or proposed CAD first and repeat
the downstream reviews.
Who decides
Fix ordinary camera and modelling errors directly. If the view depends on hiding a disputed
door or adopting a different arrangement, hold it and take the design choice back to the
homeowner.

g.aria-label: Products · Do the variants, lighting and palette pass together?
g.text: PRODUCTS
Do the variants, lighting and palette pass together?
Reconcile every selected or reused shopping ID, quantity, exact variant and dimensions against the reopened
native objects. Check out-of-frame items separately. Compare supplier references in neutral light, then
inspect the same camera under the proposed lighting. Record a room-palette finding for every furnished room.
Tools in use
Blender compares the actual variants, lighting and palette with the shopping schedule. Colour
Expert can help resolve open choices. An optional AI styling study can inform sourcing.
Proceed
Pass products with the current evidence.
Check-render for final-ai against the actual
input revision and any explicit AI hold before
sending the reviewed camera and product
references to the image editor.
Hold, correct and return
Correct a wrong material, variant, count or light
in the scene and repeat the camera and product
checks. If a substitute changes fit, return to
CAD. If identity cannot be verified, keep the
affected finish view on hold.
Who decides
If a consequential palette choice remains, show the options under consistent light. Record the
owner’s choice or delegated decision and repeat the furnished-room palette check. A suggested
minor improvement can accompany a pass.

g.aria-label: Final AI · Does this photo match this exact camera?
g.text: FINAL AI
Does this photo match this exact camera?
Compare each generated photo beside its reviewed Blender camera and product references. Compare the intended
door mechanism with both views. Inspect seat access, counts, fronts, clearances, finishes, lighting and
colours. Record an ai-colour finding per issued camera.
Tools in use
Reference-image editing uses the checked Blender camera and product references. Compare the
photograph beside that camera and run check-room-photos on the required views.
Proceed
Pass final-ai for that camera and take the
reviewed pair into the commissioned presentation.
Keep rejected images outside the issue.
Hold, correct and return
Retry image-only drift from the original reviewed
camera. For a scene or product error, fix Blender
and repeat the product and camera checks. For
wrong fabric or an incorrect arrangement, return
to CAD and recheck dependent work.
Who decides
If the owner wants an idea introduced by the AI, record the choice, source and model it,
recheck fit where affected, then generate a new final photo.
Issue, shared costs and later work

g.aria-label: Consent · What evidence permits this alteration to advance?
g.text: CONSENT
What evidence permits this alteration to advance?
A new opening, change of use, frontage, boundary or shared service can trigger an enquiry. Match the plot,
nation, authority, proposal revision, relevant rights, decision notices and conditions. Check the
building-control route for the actual intervention.
Tools in use
Renovation Pack uses the nation-specific consent enquiry, authority records and the proposed
FreeCAD drawing to identify which permissions and replies the alteration needs.
Proceed
Record the dated evidence, its status and
permitted next use. A buyer can receive the
outstanding enquiries. Carry any actual
permission and its conditions into the
coordinated design and programme.
Buyer assessment
Hold, correct and return
If the plot, decision or condition is uncertain,
request the record and hold dependent
commitments. If the design changes, revisit the
applicable enquiry, cost and affected rooms.
Who decides
The planning authority, building-control professional, solicitor or surveyor resolves the
specific question. Ask the homeowner whether to pursue a permitted alternative only when that
choice changes the design or spend.

g.aria-label: Decorator · Is each requested surface ready to specify?
g.text: DECORATOR
Is each requested surface ready to specify?
This branch can start from the brief independently of renders. Check one entry per scoped surface,
manufacturer, named colour, finish, code where supplied, revision and sample approval or explicit
instruction. Run check-decorator on that revision and surface scope.
Tools in use
Colour Expert and the surface schedule bring together shade, sheen, sample and approval. Run
house.py check-decorator before issuing finishes.
Proceed
Issue the approved surface schedule. A concept
can separately identify outstanding sample
decisions.
Decorator issue
Hold, correct and return
Hold a surface with a missing specification or
sample decision. Compare the physical sample
against retained finishes in the relevant light,
update the schedule and repeat the scoped check.
Who decides
The homeowner or delegated approver confirms the physical finish where a sample is required.
Record the actual approval before issuing instructions for that surface.

g.aria-label: Whole house · Can the affected package be priced, ordered or phased?
g.text: WHOLE HOUSE
Can the affected package be priced, ordered or phased?
Track shared structure, services, consent, surveys, costs and occupancy on the dashboard. Use the same
revision for tender comparisons. Reconcile VAT, exclusions, provisional sums, delivery, substitutions and
reserve. Check access, cooking, WC, washing and heat in each affected phase.
Tools in use
Renovation Pack connects affected rooms, shared routes, quotes, orders and budget. Python
tender comparisons and a shopping workbook reconcile quantities, exclusions and allowances.
Proceed
Carry the approved scope and outstanding holds to
the budget, shopping list, bidders and programme.
Release a dependent order only with its required
measurements, decisions and procurement
authority.
Priced package
Hold, correct and return
A changed pier, price, delivery or service
handover can reopen several rooms. Update
impacted drawings and orders, rerun routes,
reprice like for like and reschedule dependent
trades. Unaffected work can continue.
Who decides
Ask about budget or occupation when it changes the viable options. “Must you stay here
throughout, and which facilities must work each night?” The engineer, installer or authority
resolves technical or consent questions.

g.aria-label: Handover · Can each recipient open and rely on the issue?
g.text: HANDOVER
Can each recipient open and rely on the issue?
Inspect the actual exported drawings and presentation. Reopen the native files, test the named camera where
commissioned, compare image pairs, reconcile quantities and costs, extract the archive and check the
recipient’s scope.
Tools in use
Use house.py checklist and save-revision to issue the reviewed work. For a photo pack,
check-room-photos and check-house-photos verify the evidence, then pack-house-photos assembles
it. PDF and workbook tools prepare the recipient files.

a.aria-label: Open the separate pack delivery workflow

g.text: Proceed
Check each visible window covering, including its
outside face through other windows. Verify the
final photo against its camera and its bytes
inside the room pack before inviting another
study. Carry purchase-only holds to the shopping
schedule. For an expressly shorter commission,
deliver its checked buyer, CAD, camera or
decorator output. Refresh CHECKLIST.md with the
reviewed outputs, homeowner acceptance and owners
of outstanding returns.
Issued pack
Hold, correct and return
If a file, image, price, revision or quantity
disagrees, return to its owning stage, correct it
and reopen affected reviews. For a survey return,
link the measurement and the repeated design
check in the survey register. Repackage, extract
and examine the issue again. Keep a withdrawn
issue identifiable.
Affected review
Who decides
Show the issued work and use the [handover question
guidance](../skills/renovation-pack/references/homeowner-decisions.md#at-the-end-of-a-commission).
Invite a reaction to a review or ask about the specific choice that blocks progress. Record
their reply and follow an existing instruction.

g.aria-label: Occupied works · Is the next construction phase ready?
g.text: OCCUPIED WORKS
Is the next construction phase ready?
Apply this branch when the appointment covers the works. Test the facilities the household needs, including
the actual route to them at the time of use. Identify shared isolations, deliveries, access and any temporary
arrangement.
Tools in use
The local Python programme checks facilities and access night by night. Use OpenProject for
trade dependencies when the project workspace is available.
Proceed
Once the plumber or trade demonstrates the
handover and the household can use the facility,
release the dependent phase. Record what was
demonstrated, by whom and what remains open.
Next phase
Hold, correct and return
If the working bathroom, safe access, heat or
another agreed facility is unavailable, delay the
dependent strip-out. Rebook the trade or price
temporary arrangements and send the change back
to the budget and programme.
Who decides
The site lead verifies access and the trade verifies the service. Ask the homeowner whether a
proposed interruption or nights away are acceptable when a workable sequence depends on that
choice.

g.aria-label: Completion · Is the installed result recorded and usable?
g.text: COMPLETION
Is the installed result recorded and usable?
When appointed through construction, reconcile installed work with the approved variation, as-built drawing,
commissioning results, warranties, controls and access for maintenance. Inspect outstanding snags with their
owners.
Tools in use
Renovation Pack reconciles as-built returns, commissioned tests, warranties and snags. FreeCAD
records verified changes. The checklist and revision history retain the accepted issue.
Proceed
Hand over the usable owner records, status of
outstanding works and maintenance information.
Close an individual snag after its correction has
been checked.
Owner records
Hold, correct and return
An as-built discrepancy, failed test or
inaccessible control returns to its designer or
installer. Update the record, repeat the affected
test and reissue corrected owner information.
Affected review
Who decides
The responsible installer or professional verifies the work. The homeowner decides any
material change of scope, cost or finish through the recorded variation process.
What calls for a specialist?

svg.text: Screen new instructions, follow-ups and findings from other rooms. Use the study if its answer could
change the decision. Check permissions, run linked studies where needed, then return to the affected

g.text: “Take me through the house and
show me the view when I sit
down.”
Use the Blender house walkthrough only when
someone requests a first-person visit, in
ordinary language or by skill name.
Give the homeowner the requested
playable tour or navigable
scene. Routine room checks and
brochure tours keep their
existing outputs.
A conservatory, sunroom,
glazed extension or roof-lit
room enters review.
Register north against the actual building.
Trace sun at the intended viewpoint against
dated tree, roof and terrain heights.
Compare glare, summer heat and winter cold
under the relevant use and controls.
Record the four current
findings, seasonal use,
furniture and shade choice with
their evidence and survey owner.
Glazed rooms
“Can we open up the kitchen?”
A wall moves, an opening
widens or a post appears on a
returned plan.
FreeCAD and TechDraw overlay both floors and
section the opening. Ask the engineer for
the load path, finished supports and head
height. PyNite or FEM with CalculiX can
support a commissioned analysis with
verified inputs.
Insert the support, rerun
occupied layouts, check cabinet
set-out, tender scope and
sequence.
“Could the sink go under that
window?” A duct, drain, joist,
floor level or fitting moves.
FreeCAD sections compare falls,
penetrations, outlet positions and service
access. An installer or surveyor verifies
the concealed connection. Inspect supplied
IFC units and placement with IfcOpenShell
where relevant.
Update the service drawing,
occupied fit and purchase or
trade hold.
“Can Dad get to the shower?” A
chair pulls back, a buggy
turns or a doorway changes.
FreeCAD tests the person or aid, operating
envelopes and connected thresholds. Shapely
and NetworkX compare the whole occupied
journey.
Record the pinch or deciding
site measurement. Retest the
adjoining room and each affected
activity.
“Can everyone see the TV?” A
chair turns, an opening frames
a neighbour or a garden seat
loses privacy.
FreeCAD checks all intended viewpoints,
target, natural fronts and moving people. An
authorised Blender viewport compares the
same eye position across options.
Return placements to CAD. Review
sightline, conversation, reach
and passage together.
“Where can we sit in the
evening sun?” A roof, hedge,
window or neighbouring
obstruction changes.
Establish true north, time, site levels and
obstruction heights. Use QGIS or dated LiDAR
for terrain, then Blender Sun Position or
pvlib for seasonal comparisons.
Return the shadow or sightline
to the seat, window or garden
option. Survey any height that
could reverse it.
“Will these doors make the
room too hot?” Insulation,
glazing, shading, moisture or
ventilation changes.
Review the section, fabric condition,
airflow and use. Compare indoor conditions
with EnergyPlus if weather, fabric and
operating inputs support it. Seek a survey
or building-services design where needed.
Revisit glazing, shading,
ventilation, build-up or heating
decisions and the occupied
dimensions.
“Is there room for solar
panels?” A rooflight competes
for a sunny roof face.
Check roof pitch, aspect, usable area and
shading. Compare module fit, then pvlib
generation. For savings add household demand
timing, tariffs and an installed price.
Return the roof layout, yield
range and assumptions to the
roof decision and budget.
“Could this patio be level?” A
threshold, external level,
boundary or outfall changes.
Survey levels to a common datum. Trace water
to an evidenced outfall and check access.
Match any map, aerial view or terrain data
to the actual plot.
Recheck the threshold section,
garden route and drainage
enquiry before pricing.
“Can the garage become a gym?”
The footprint, frontage, use
or work near a boundary
changes.
Renovation-pack identifies the nation and
authority. Check plot, past decisions,
conditions, other rights and the technical
building-control enquiry against the
proposed drawing.
Record dated evidence, who must
reply and what survey, design,
spend or order depends on it.
“Will music disturb a call
upstairs?” A partition, door,
noisy appliance or extract
route changes.
Trace likely sound and flanking paths,
compare simultaneous uses and arrange a
listening trial or acoustic advice if it
changes the choice.
Return the finding to room use,
door or fabric detail and any
affected ventilation.
“Make the room feel warmer.” A
paint, upholstery, reused
piece or lighting condition
changes.
Blender compares the fixed products in the
same camera and in neutral light. Use
color-expert for open choices or casts. Use
an early styling image only within scope.
Record the palette decision.
Recheck the furnished camera,
the final photo and any affected
physical finish.
“Show me how it will look.” A
camera, product substitution,
shopping variant or quantity
changes.
Blender interiors dresses and counts the
selected items, checks clearances, assets
and camera transfer. For final photography,
edit the reviewed camera with the product
references and inspect the result beside it.
Return fit errors to CAD, scene
errors to Blender and image-only
drift to the image editor.
“Which paint do I tell the
decorator to buy?” A sample,
sheen or finish instruction
changes.
Review each scheduled surface, manufacturer,
shade, sheen and recorded approval. Inspect
physical samples where required and run
check-decorator for the requested scope.
Issue approved surfaces and keep
outstanding choices visible to
the homeowner.
“Can we stay here while it is
built?” A shared isolation,
delivery or delayed trade
changes the sequence.
Renovation-pack maps essential facilities,
occupied access and service handovers night
by night. Use a phase table or OpenProject
when a programme is commissioned.
Update the programme and
temporary living costs. Hold a
dependent strip-out until the
facility works.
“What will it be worth after
alteration?”
Valuation study records the unpriced house
specification, measured or provisional area,
recent sales, listing condition and local UK
HPI.
Return the reconciled range and
evidence gaps to the feasibility
pack.
“Does this quote cover the
same job?” A supplier
substitutes a unit or a
builder excludes an item.
Reconcile quantities, dimensions,
installation, exclusions, VAT, lead times
and reserve on a common drawing and scope.
Update budget and procurement. A
substitution reopens affected
fit, product and camera reviews.
“What should we check before
buying?” A survey, new
instruction or as-built return
contradicts the issue.
Renovation-pack identifies the uncertainty
that could change the decision and routes it
to the relevant surveyor, designer,
installer or authority. At completion,
reconcile commissioned tests, snags and
warranties.
Issue a prioritised enquiry or
reopen affected rooms, orders
and records. Report what is
still usable.
Worked example · A support beam over the kitchen opening

g.aria-label: Opening enquiry · What does the engineer need to return?
g.text: OPENING ENQUIRY
What does the engineer need to return?
“Can we open the kitchen up?” triggers a structural review even if nobody mentions a beam. Overlay the
affected storeys and cut a section through the proposed opening. Identify the upper wall, floor and roof,
unknown bearings, supports below, cabinets and routes.
Tools in use
FreeCAD BIM and TechDraw overlay the storeys and section the opening. For a commissioned
analysis with verified inputs, PyNite models the beam or frame and FreeCAD FEM runs CalculiX to
inspect stress and deflection. Return support dimensions to the occupied plan.
Proceed
Send the measured-survey and opening enquiry to
the engineer. Request the finished positions and
sizes of piers or posts and the clear height
below the beam. Put the returned geometry into
both daily and eight-person layouts.
Engineer enquiry
Hold, correct and return
Where the support position or load path is
unresolved, hold the dependent set-out, kitchen
order and coordinated pricing until the return is
checked.
Who decides
The engineer establishes how the load will be carried. If the returned design conflicts with
dining or storage, the homeowner chooses between the permitted layout changes after seeing
their consequences.

g.aria-label: Orchard House · What changes after a support is returned?
g.text: ORCHARD HOUSE
What changes after a support is returned?
In the fictional replay the pier face moves 300 mm west. The occupied route drops to 646 mm for four and
eight diners against the household’s 825 mm serving target. Withdraw the old cabinet set-out from pricing.
Tools in use
FreeCAD MCP inserts the returned pier. Shapely and NetworkX retest the occupied route. The
tender comparison and bathroom programme carry the resulting cost and timing into the house
decision.
Proceed
Shorten the end unit, shift the table and move
the dry prep bench. At R3 the routes reach 945 mm
for four and 845 mm for eight. Take the storage
choice to the owner, send both bidders the same
plan and check the site before ordering.
Priced package
Hold, correct and return
Shortening the cabinet alone restores a 950 mm
straight gap, yet eight diners still leave only
666 mm on the continuous route. Repeat the
occupied test at each change. Carry the selected
scope and any cost of staying at home into the
tender comparison.
Who decides
“Would you move the displaced storage to the utility?” In the separate fictional beam
benchmark, the hand check and PyNite give 0.91553 mm of midspan movement. The fine CalculiX
mesh gives 0.91868 mm. A live beam design requires the engineer’s site-specific inputs and
interpretation.

svg.text: Orchard House · The occupied return path
Fictional pier return. Follow the serving route past eight diners as the kitchen changes.
